## Capability work is missing from the attempt budget

Status: in-progress. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The attempt resource receipt measures the provider process. It does not exclusively own and account for all capability, browser, adapter, and completion work that Buster launches.

A cheap provider can report low resource usage while its other local work exceeds the claimed CPU, memory or process budget.

### Components and current state

- Buster Runner
- Provider process
- Capability RPC
- Report adapters
- Shared Worker Core

Core now performs early and final resource observations. runner.measure still reads instance.resources(); moving the observation later does not create exclusive whole-attempt ownership. Durable fixture readiness/control, separate readiness/completion promises, a bounded fourth process pipe and native launcher ownership primitives exist as locally tested building blocks. The production runner still constructs LocalWorkerRuntime; the native lifetime API is not its production execution path.

### Remaining work

- Integrate durable attempt/claim-bound local execution ownership across Core and Buster, including provider work, parent capability execution, browser/command children, adapters, evidence and finalization.
- Define aggregate measurement and hard budget enforcement. Distinguish cumulative CPU from CPU rate and processes from cgroup tasks. Required missing observations must fail. Declare remote BuildKit/Kubernetes work separately.
- Preserve retained fixtures through durable ownership transfer, fences and crash recovery; coordinate with the restarted-job workspace recovery issue in this register.
- Connect the actual Buster attempt host, restricted role-specific launch policy/broker and durable fixture lifetime to the runner. Keep broker and capability work inside the attempt scope. After the verified cutover remove the superseded executable runner, file-capability launch and sampling paths; retain no executable fallback.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run the original provider in an actual delegated cgroup. Keep its own load small and launch two real capability children whose combined load exceeds the attempt budget although individual limits pass.
- Put load separately in the report adapter and finalization. Compare the original receipt and terminal state with aggregate counters; unrelated concurrent service work must not be charged to this attempt.
- Exercise short-lived children, descendants surviving their leader, missing counters, cancellation and drain failure. Fake cgroup files are not positive containment evidence.

### Completion criteria

- Every claimed local phase has exclusive ownership or demonstrably non-overlapping equivalent accounting.
- Aggregate overrun or missing required observations prevent completed; successful drain leaves no local work running.
- Original Core/Buster claim, timeout, fixture and evidence guarantees remain covered.
- Fixture readiness is journaled before dependency acknowledgement, teardown fences acknowledgement races, and only the original Core terminal journal seals completion. Historical readiness cannot authorize new dependents.

### Separate environment acceptance

Actual delegated cgroups and real providers/browsers are required. Acceptance in the deployed worker container is separate.

### Dependencies

- [Restarted terminal jobs retain source workspaces without a durable quiescence proof](#restarted-terminal-jobs-retain-source-workspaces-without-a-durable-quiescence-proof)

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned implementation establishes the ownership gap. No test rerun or live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** No execution result is available for this evidence boundary.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

## Restarted terminal jobs retain source workspaces without a durable quiescence proof

Status: partially-implemented. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

After a worker or host crash there is no durable proof that every process belonging to a job has stopped. Source and working directories therefore remain retained.

Repeated interrupted jobs can consume disk and quotas. Deleting from terminal metadata alone could remove inputs still used by live descendants.

### Components and current state

- Buster RemotePlanService
- terminal-workspace
- Provider/capability/adapter ownership

Normal confirmed execution cleans inputs. Durable status write and read failures stop admission; shutdown waits for pending admission writes. recover() explicitly retains inputs because a terminal record does not prove orphan quiescence.

### Remaining work

- Publish durable job/attempt/claim ownership before launch and include capability children, adapters and retained fixtures.
- On restart reconcile the exact fenced owner and require authoritative complete termination. Preserve and diagnose unknown ownership instead of guessing.
- Authorize the existing narrow idempotent input cleanup only after that proof; preserve valid result, evidence and log receipts.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Crash and restart the original worker with a live provider plus actual capability/adapter children. Distinguish leader death from complete process termination.
- Exercise crash windows around ownership publication, drain and file removal; reused or namespace-mismatched PIDs must never authorize cleanup.
- Read completed/failed/cancelled job receipts and retained-fixture transitions after restart.

### Completion criteria

- No active or uncertain owner loses its inputs.
- After complete quiescence is proved, only authorized inputs are removed; repeated recovery is safe.
- Real quota release and retained result/evidence access are demonstrated on original jobs.

### Separate environment acceptance

Native crash and containment tests are required. Log retention and external demo lifetime are independent of source-workspace cleanup.

### Dependencies

- [Capability work is missing from the attempt budget](#capability-work-is-missing-from-the-attempt-budget)

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned implementation establishes the remaining quiescence gap. Local checks cover only the bounded behavior described below; no live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** Partial. Buster records both a failed durable terminal-status write and an actual status-read failure as fatal service errors, preserving both causes. Shutdown waits for active admission work. The quota, lock and corruption suite passed all 7 checks. A separate suite passed all 6 checks, and the type check passed. Data remains unchanged.
- **implementation commit:** 550eb948ec8766b38e8c8d4ccb88a1fdab28e61a

## Confirmed run history lacks complete connected retirement

Status: partially-implemented. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

Confirmed history still lacks a complete release protocol understood by every reader and component that can reopen, accept or replay it.

Partial compaction can leave record, metadata, evidence and blob quotas exhausted. Uncoordinated deletion could lose evidence or protection against repeated external actions.

### Components and current state

- RecordStore
- Attempt/Admission
- ArtifactStore
- Buster jobs
- Nova dispatch/import
- Operator delivery

Telemetry, admission, imported attempt results, redundant dispatch archive copies and causal operator projections have bounded implementations and local evidence. They do not remove all job counts, evidence objects or shared blobs. The dispatch projection has a real one-POST replay result while retaining logical job, receipt and source blob. Its native provider execution failed; that failure does not invalidate the bounded storage transition or prove successful native execution.

### Remaining work

- Inventory active/completed owners, all current reopen/accept/read/replay consumers and shared references.
- Implement explicit manual release with durable consumer completion and required idempotency/uncertainty tombstones, atomically across those consumers. Keep every still-required reference resolvable.
- Release actual byte and record quotas rather than moving data into unaccounted sidecars. D07 does not permit automatic age-based log deletion.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Use small real store quotas with active, waiting and completed runs and shared artifacts; measure actual bytes and entries before/after authorized release.
- Replay old deliveries after restart and exercise competing writers and SIGKILL between durable transitions.
- Use original result, evidence, artifact and operator readers on retired and deliberately retained history.

### Completion criteria

- Only authorized and fully confirmed history is released; active and uncertain work remains intact.
- Released capacity admits new actual writes. Replays do not repeat an external action or fabricate delivery outcomes.
- All affected consumers understand the same retirement state and retain the existing projection guarantees.

### Separate environment acceptance

Original local store/process tests can close this implementation scope. Cleanup of real user data remains a separate operational action.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned implementation establishes the remaining connected-retirement gap. No new test rerun or live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** Partial: telemetry, admission and imported attempt-result copies were checked with actual quota release and preserved replay. The attempt-v2 suite passed all 19 checks. The integrated suite passed all 45 checks with no skips. Complete retention across the remaining stores and references remains open.
- **implementation commit:** 27315faad862f71df940ed32bc4e5a98eca72e0d

## Runtime image rebuild inputs are not fully reproducible

Status: in-progress. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

A source commit still does not bind all browser archives and time-dependent scanner databases; complete image rebuilds have not been compared.

The same source can produce different installed content or scan results. Source pinning does not guarantee byte-identical images.

### Components and current state

- versions.json
- Runtime Dockerfiles
- Playwright downloads
- Trivy databases

Python transitive locks, Go modules, binary checksums and apt snapshots have partial fixes backed by real installations/builds. ARM64 wheel resolution is not ARM64 execution. Complete image builds and browser launches remain outstanding.

### Remaining work

- Bind browser archives to independently verified hashes. Preserve Trivy refresh data as explicit reproducible inputs while recording scan freshness separately.
- Define architecture and builder/provenance inputs, then compare two complete isolated builds from identical selections.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- RUNTIME_LOCK_PYTHON="$PYTHON_311" node --test tests/verification/deployment/runtime-tool-locks-native.mjs
- RUNTIME_LOCK_GO="$SELECTED_GO" node --test tests/verification/deployment/go-tool-locks-native.mjs
- Build complete images twice with independent empty caches and identical source, architecture, browser/database bytes and builder settings. Compare package inventory, SBOM and output digests.

### Completion criteria

- All remaining time-dependent inputs are explicitly bound.
- Two actual complete builds exist; every package/SBOM/digest difference is explained against the selected rebuild contract.
- Actual selected browsers and tools execute. Claim ARM64 runtime support only after actual ARM64 execution.

### Separate environment acceptance

Complete isolated image/browser tests are required. Deployment of verified output digests and ARM64 live acceptance remain separate.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned build inputs establish the reproducibility gap. No test rerun or live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** Partial fix locally verified; the complete finding remains open
- **implementation commit:** 2ed91ef75e4c18b0a6b95b6d2850739b3c38ebf4

## Operator configuration is not fully separated from public examples

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

Operator-specific values and routing/identity assumptions are not consistently separated from a complete generic public configuration interface.

Other users may inherit unsuitable operator values. Dockerignore prevents neither Git publication nor historical exposure; this finding does not establish a secret leak.

### Components and current state

- my-values
- gitops/production/overlays
- Chart values
- Installation documentation

Operator-specific configuration still requires separation from public examples. Actual values are referenced by path rather than copied into this register.

### Remaining work

- Separate operator configuration from fully parameterized fictional examples; document namespace, routing, identity and external-secret interfaces.
- Inspect current Git/build/artifact scope and relevant history for sensitive leftovers and report precise search limits. A history rewrite needs its own concrete decision.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Clone the intended public surface without private configuration and render complete examples using fictional IDs and secret placeholders.
- Inspect Git files, relevant history, Docker build context and produced artifacts separately; never copy real secret values into the report.

### Completion criteria

- A fresh clone supports a usable anonymous configuration path without real operator identities.
- Required parameters and external secrets are complete; retained private values have explicit ownership.
- Secret inspection states its exact scope and outcome; a sample search is not a blanket secret-free conclusion.

## Long-lived rootless BuildKit lacks a job-specific process boundary

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The long-lived rootless BuildKit uses --net=host and --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox; the missing process sandbox is an unresolved security boundary for untrusted Dockerfile RUN work.

Project code may affect the shared build process environment or leave processes running. Supervisor secret access or privilege escalation has not been demonstrated.

### Components and current state

- Buster runtime
- rootlesskit/BuildKit
- Build provider
- Shared cache

Both flags remain in docker/buster-runtime-entrypoint.sh. Rootless UID/file permissions and a separate supervisor identity do not by themselves provide the missing job process boundary.

### Remaining work

- Run untrusted builds in an ephemeral dedicated security/process boundary, outside long-lived control and credential processes.
- Define connected cache/file/network access and cleanup guarantees for the exact pinned runtime image.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Using the real runtime image, execute two distinct build jobs and negatively test unauthorized process visibility, signals and background processes surviving job completion.
- Test cross-job file/cache access and unauthorized network egress. A successful rootless startup probe is insufficient.

### Completion criteria

- Build jobs cannot influence unrelated control/job processes or continue after confirmed completion.
- Allowed cache/network paths and forbidden cross-job access are demonstrated with real builds.

### Separate environment acceptance

Isolated native security tests on the pinned image are required; accept the actual host/container boundary separately.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned service definition establishes the process-boundary gap. No test rerun or live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** No execution result is available for this evidence boundary.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

## Automated host bootstrap and restore prerequisites are incomplete

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The repository setup assumes an existing cluster; the effective host/K3s/storage starting environment is not a fully reproducible bootstrap and restore contract.

After host loss or on a new host, versions, datastore, disk and application dependencies must be reconstructed. The setup name alone can overstate its coverage.

### Components and current state

- K3s/host
- Host bootstrap automation
- scripts/deploy.sh
- Storage provisioner
- Paperless dependencies

Installation and setup documents start from an existing cluster. The repository has no supported empty-host automation. It cannot install and configure K3s, establish storage and independent access, or emit a reproducible host record. The repository records no effective cluster configuration, and generic K3s defaults do not replace actual operator settings.

### Remaining work

- Record redacted actual host/K3s versions, startup flags, datastore, API requirements, CNI, StorageClass/CSI and cgroup preparation.
- Implement one reviewed, idempotent host-bootstrap entry point with prerequisite checks, a dry-run or plan view, explicit stop conditions and bounded rollback before irreversible changes.
- Automate the selected K3s, datastore, DNS, CNI, storage and independent-administration preparation without storing credentials in Git or combining an unproved CNI migration with application deployment.
- Emit a redacted machine-readable record of effective versions, flags, network ranges, storage ownership and recovery inputs.
- Hand off to scripts/deploy.sh only after the platform checks pass.
- Document host backup, key/credential ownership, Paperless dependencies and independent administration with a restore sequence.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- On an isolated empty host, use only the completed documented procedure.
- After restore verify API, DNS, storage, pipeline and required Paperless data; treat every undocumented prerequisite supplied manually as a gap.

### Completion criteria

- Another operator can use the reviewed automation and documented external inputs to build the selected cluster from an empty supported host without undocumented manual preparation.
- A repeated run is safe, the plan and effective host record are reviewable, and every irreversible action has a stated stop and recovery boundary.
- The automated handoff deploys no application until API, DNS, storage, identity prerequisites and independent administration pass.
- An isolated host-loss exercise restores the selected environment and its data; host/cluster ownership, supported version boundaries and verified recovery results are complete.

### Separate environment acceptance

An isolated empty host and real restore media are required. The current repository does not provision this cluster; the future automation and restore exercise must provide the evidence.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The pinned automation establishes the bootstrap and restore gap. No test rerun or live environment result is available.

- **Observed behavior:** No execution result is available for this evidence boundary.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

## Continuous GitOps health compares a branch name with resolved commit IDs

Status: open. Severity: unassessed.

### Problem and impact

continuousApplications sets runtime child targetRevision=main, but strict application-health.lua requires status.sync.revision and operationState.syncResult.revision to equal that literal targetRevision. A resolved commit SHA does not equal main.

An actually synchronized healthy runtime child reporting its SHA can remain Progressing in the app-of-apps gate and block later waves. This is a source-confirmed mismatch, not an observed live outage.

### Components and current state

- scripts/gitops-continuous.mjs
- charts/gitops/files/application-health.lua
- Runtime app-of-apps

The pinned implementation compares the configured branch name with resolved commit IDs. Existing health tests cover exact commit pins, stale-operation rejection and separate observed platform mode, but contain no positive continuous main-with-resolved-SHA case.

### Remaining work

- Bind the selected and actually synchronized immutable revision consistently while continuous manifests track main.
- Preserve stale-operation, source-path, destination, error and drift checks. Removing revision comparisons or switching runtime children to observed mode is not sufficient.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Invoke the original Lua with spec.source.targetRevision="main", status.sync.status="Synced", status.sync.revision="aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", health.status="Healthy", operationState.phase="Succeeded" and syncResult.revision set to that same SHA. comparedTo.source must match spec.source including main/path/repoURL/directory.include; comparedTo.destination must match spec.destination. Omit observed mode. Current code returns Progressing.
- Use the immutable-SHA positive fixture in tests/verification/deployment/gitops-health.test.mjs and change only spec.source.targetRevision and comparedTo.source.targetRevision to main. Test current and stale operation revisions separately.

### Completion criteria

- The selected real continuous commit can reach Healthy when sync, source binding, successful operation and workload health all match it.
- Stale or mismatched successful operations remain blocked; ComparisonError, drift, changed paths and destination changes retain their protections.
- Runtime and manually synchronized platform health remain separate contracts.

### Separate environment acceptance

After correction, accept an actual branch-to-SHA rollout with the subsequent wave and a stale operation. Lua fixtures alone do not establish live acceptance.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The inspection covered both original sources and the existing health test. Deterministic mismatch follows from string comparison. No Lua or Argo execution occurred.

## Uncertain external effects have no supported reconciliation and result-import operation

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

Effect recovery correctly stops when an external service accepts a request without returning a trustworthy receipt. It also stops when a receipt exists without terminal attempt evidence. The current platform supplies no supported operation that records reconciliation and imports the authoritative result.

An operator can identify an uncertain effect but cannot continue the run through a documented, validated state transition. Blind retry can duplicate an external mutation, while journal editing would bypass lifecycle authority.

### Components and current state

- Nova effect recovery
- Administrative retry and remediation
- External capability adapters
- Effectful extension path

Source tracing followed the recovery guard through normal execution and administrative retry. Both paths stop on unresolved external outcomes. The effectful guide states this limit and does not invent a continuation command.

### Remaining work

- Define a versioned reconciliation request and result contract with actor identity, effect identity, evidence, idempotency and authorization.
- Implement one Core-owned operation that records the decision and imports or compensates the result without editing journals.
- Add failure, duplicate, cancellation, restart and audit tests, then document the supported operator and extension behavior.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run the persistent external-effect recovery tests in the verification record.
- Create an accepted external effect without a receipt, then attempt normal resume and administrative retry. Observe that both paths return the unresolved-outcome guard.
- Inspect skills/nova/core/execution/effect-recovery.ts, engine-run.ts and engine-admin.ts. Confirm that no supported reconciliation import operation follows the stop.

### Completion criteria

- An authorized operator can reconcile one uncertain effect through a supported API without direct journal changes.
- The operation rejects mismatched effect, attempt, actor and evidence identities and remains idempotent after restart.
- The effectful extension guide includes the exact operation, observations, failure paths and retained evidence.

### Separate environment acceptance

Local contract and restart tests can prove the state transition. A real external service remains a separate live acceptance exercise.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

Independent source trace and local recovery exercises; no reconciliation implementation was added.

- **Observed behavior:** Normal, retry and remediation paths all preserve the recovery stop.

## Prism OpenClaw tools lack general payload and request-lifetime limits

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The Prism OpenClaw extension bounds the number of designs but does not define general text or document size limits. Its HTTP request also has no explicit timeout or cancellation signal.

A large request or stalled Prism control connection can retain host resources for an undefined period. Extension authors cannot copy a complete bounded-call pattern from this package.

### Components and current state

- Prism OpenClaw extension
- Prism control client
- Host extension guidance

The schemas constrain design count but do not set complete text or document limits. The HTTP call has no explicit timeout or cancellation signal.

### Remaining work

- Approve explicit request-size, text-size and document-size limits for both Prism tools.
- Add an explicit timeout and cancellation propagation contract to the HTTP call.
- Test boundary values, cancellation, timeout, host registration and error mapping, then update the package page.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Inspect skills/prism/openclaw-plugin/index.mjs and identify the design-count constraint.
- Confirm that the parameter schemas do not set complete text/document bounds and that the fetch call has no timeout or cancellation signal.
- Run the current registration tests and observe that they check names and design count, not a real host request lifetime.

### Completion criteria

- Approved schemas bound all request-controlled payloads or record a justified alternative resource boundary.
- The client enforces a documented timeout and propagates cancellation without committing a partial revision.
- Tests exercise limits and real host registration, and the host-extension guide states the verified behavior.

### Separate environment acceptance

Local schema and cancellation tests are required first. A real OpenClaw-to-Prism call remains separate live evidence.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

Independent source and registration-test inspection; no product implementation changed.

- **Observed behavior:** The package registration test passed but did not establish a bounded real-host request.

### Sources

- [skills/prism/openclaw-plugin/index.mjs](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/bcf032f241b432bf920baa9ee5f727947921447d/skills/prism/openclaw-plugin/index.mjs) — The tool schemas and HTTP request show the current count, payload and request-lifetime behavior.

## Prism spike tests require an unavailable fixed browser path

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The mobile-editor and preview-isolation Playwright configurations require the absolute Chromium headless-shell build 1228 path. Their locked Playwright 1.55.0 installations select build 1187. The root Prism Playwright 1.62.1 installation selects build 1234. Neither spike configuration selects the installed package browser or accepts a path override.

Ordinary locked dependency and Chromium installation does not prepare these two browser test suites. The complete local Prism checks stop at the mobile spike; downstream checks in the same aggregate do not run. This failure does not establish a runtime Studio defect.

### Components and current state

- Prism mobile-editor spike
- Prism preview-isolation spike
- Prism maintainers: browser test configuration and supported verification environment

At source revision ec2a42ed215a2fa7dbd3172ef70ef446084963a9, the fixed path remains in both configurations. Independent local execution completed locked bootstrap and all three package-local browser installations, then still failed before browser launch: twelve mobile tests and three preview tests. The implementation provides no supported browser-path override.

### Remaining work

- Prism maintainers must replace the fixed path with a supported browser selection or provide and validate a compatible immutable managed browser installation.
- Until a supported installation exists, stop when the required executable is absent. Preserve the command, source revision and launch error; do not substitute a different browser build through a symlink.
- Keep individual checks that can run separate from failed aggregate results. Do not classify this local launch failure as deferred live validation.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- From a clean checkout at the stated revision, run npm ci and npm run bootstrap:prism:tests using the documented prerequisites.
- Install Chromium with the local Playwright CLI in skills/prism, spikes/prism/mobile-editor and spikes/prism/preview-isolation. Record each package version and selected browser build.
- Run npm run verify --prefix spikes/prism/mobile-editor and npm run verify --prefix spikes/prism/preview-isolation. If the fixed 1228 executable is absent, both fail before launch despite completed installation.
- Run npm run verify:prism. Its spike stage fails before later aggregate stages. verify:prism:repository and verify:prism:production begin with that same aggregate.

### Completion criteria

- A clean documented supported environment resolves a compatible executable for each spike without ad hoc path aliases or configuration edits.
- Both original spike verifiers pass with their locked dependency trees and selected browser versions recorded.
- The original verify:prism and verify:prism:repository aggregates complete successfully; preserve stage results so unrelated later failures remain visible.
- The supported installation, host prerequisites, browser selection and failure procedure agree with the current configuration.

### Separate environment acceptance

This is a local browser-test setup defect. Its closure does not prove a live deployment, native evaluation or the full Studio-to-Nova journey. Those retain their separate environment acceptance requirements.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

Observed on 2026-10-10 at the pinned revision with unchanged product sources. Locked installs and Chromium downloads completed; the two spike launches still failed at the fixed missing path. Host library compatibility is a separate prerequisite.

- **Observed behavior:** Twelve mobile and three preview browser-launch failures after package-local Chromium installation. No successful spike browser execution or aggregate completion is claimed.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

## Platform shutdown timeout can overflow the Node timer range

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The platform schema accepts every integer shutdownTimeoutMs of at least 1 and has no maximum. Adapter deadline consumers pass the captured value to Node timers. Node.js 24.21.0 converts a delay above 2,147,483,647 milliseconds to 1 millisecond.

A schema-valid increase can sharply shorten activation or readiness waits, invocation cleanup deadlines, normal shutdown deadlines, or failed-start abort timing. A loaded or recorded value is not proof of the actual timer delay.

### Components and current state

- Nova runtime maintainers: adapter deadline consumers
- Platform configuration maintainers: validation and safe input range

At revision 9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c, no maximum is enforced by the platform schema. On 2026-10-10, the original loader accepted 2147483648 and a synthetic adapter using the original normal-shutdown consumer rejected ADAPTER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT after approximately 1.9 ms on Node.js v24.21.0. Node reported the overflow and 1 ms delay. The configuration references now require a stop outside 1–2,147,483,647 ms.

### Remaining work

- Runtime and platform configuration maintainers must define and enforce the supported timer input range at validation or the consumer boundary.
- Before consumer recreation, stop on an out-of-range value even if schema validation succeeds; retain the previous valid configuration.
- Keep rejecting deadlines separate from cleanup paths that only send an abort signal and await the adapter. A timer expiration does not prove external work stopped.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Load a complete otherwise-valid platform file with shutdownTimeoutMs set to 2147483648 using the original loadPlatformConfig; observe that validation accepts the value.
- With a synthetic adapter whose shutdown remains pending, run the original AdapterRuntime shutdown and record the timer warning and ADAPTER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT; release pending synthetic work afterwards.
- Check the boundary 2147483647 with a synthetic operation that completes before the timer, then clear the timer. Do not leave a long-running timer or claim its entire duration was measured.

### Completion criteria

- The supported input range is explicit and enforced before an unsupported value reaches a Node timer.
- Original loader and deadline-consumer tests cover the upper boundary and the first value above it, with exact assertions for acceptance or rejection.
- All consumers using the platform shutdown duration preserve their documented rejection or abort behavior; unsupported values cannot silently become a shorter deadline.
- The configuration reference, schema and consumer behavior agree at the implementing revision.

### Separate environment acceptance

Existing evidence is an original-source local loader and synthetic-adapter probe. The probe did not perform pipeline recovery, live adapter shutdown, deployed-environment checks, or cleanup of external operations.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

Observed original runtime behavior with unchanged product sources on Node.js v24.21.0; schema and consumer inspected at the pinned revision. The documented conversion agrees with [Node.js 24.21.0 timer semantics](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/timers.html#settimeoutcallback-delay-args).

- **Observed behavior:** Overflow and boundary probes passed their behavioral assertions; those successes reproduce the input-range defect and do not close it. Pending synthetic operations were released.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

### Sources

- [skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json#L94-L96) — Schema requires minimum1 without a maximum.
- [skills/nova/core/execution/adapters.ts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c/skills/nova/core/execution/adapters.ts#L74-L84) — Normal shutdown passes the configured delay directly to setTimeout.
- [skills/nova/core/execution/adapter-startup.ts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c/skills/nova/core/execution/adapter-startup.ts#L144-L165) — Failed-readiness teardown and rollback use timed abort signals.
- [skills/nova/core/execution/engine-runtime.ts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-runtime.ts#L75-L87) — Consumer construction receives the platform shutdown timeout.

## Empty Cilium direction rules do not establish the intended default deny

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The checked-in dtlabs-workload-default-deny clusterwide policy has empty ingress and egress lists; hubble-ui-private has an empty ingress list. Neither contains a nonempty ingress, ingress-deny, egress or egress-deny rule. The selected Cilium 1.20.1 parser rejects such a rule before processing enableDefaultDeny.

Do not rely on these two objects as proof of workload isolation or Hubble UI ingress denial. Other independently effective policies can still apply; their actual coverage must be checked separately. Successful YAML parsing, CRD registration, apply or workload rollout does not prove enforcement of these objects.

### Components and current state

- Cilium deployment maintainers: selected controller version and policy status
- Network policy maintainers: default-deny policy intent and traffic acceptance

The deployment script selects Cilium 1.20.1 and applies the policy file at revision 9d085bb20af0cc70201cc41801011b63c626301c. The corresponding immutable Cilium implementation rejects a rule when all four rule lists are empty; both CNP and CCNP parsers call that validation. The checks did not execute a Go parser, Kubernetes admission, controller-status inspection, or traffic enforcement.

### Remaining work

- Network policy maintainers must choose a valid policy representation for the intended deny behavior on the selected Cilium version and preserve the required exceptions.
- Until that representation is independently validated, stop any release acceptance that relies on these two objects for isolation. Inspect accepted controller policy status and effective coverage rather than assuming enableDefaultDeny repairs an empty rule.
- Keep YAML/schema, Kubernetes admission, controller parsing and actual network enforcement as separate evidence classes. Do not replace an empty direction with an allow-all rule as a shortcut.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Inspect the selected version in scripts/deploy-cilium.sh and the two named objects in my-values/infra/cilium-cluster-policies.yaml.
- Against Cilium commit 7d68cfb394f2960e10aa72e76d0d51e66c1b2ebc, inspect Rule.Sanitize and the CNP/CCNP Parse calls. The empty-rule rejection precedes default-deny processing. This is a source reproduction, not an executed Go test.
- In a separately authorized representative target environment, inspect admission and controller status for both objects. Run positive and negative traffic cases for the intended workload and Hubble UI coverage.

### Completion criteria

- Both policy objects parse, and the selected controller accepts them. Retain their controller status.
- Negative traffic cases demonstrate the intended ingress/egress denial and positive cases demonstrate each required exception.
- Observed behavior is attributable to the corrected policies, with competing policies and selected endpoint labels recorded.
- Deployment instructions, generated configuration reference and policy intent match the validated implementation and controller revision.

### Separate environment acceptance

Controller parsing, admission and representative traffic tests are required for product closure. Existing evidence is source-only; no successful enforcement or actual deployment failure is claimed.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

The 1.20.1 tag resolves to commit 7d68cfb394f2960e10aa72e76d0d51e66c1b2ebc. Read [Rule.Sanitize empty-rule rejection](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/7d68cfb394f2960e10aa72e76d0d51e66c1b2ebc/pkg/policy/api/rule_validation.go#L42-L46), [CNP validation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/7d68cfb394f2960e10aa72e76d0d51e66c1b2ebc/pkg/k8s/apis/cilium.io/v2/cnp_types.go#L195-L199) and [CCNP validation](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/7d68cfb394f2960e10aa72e76d0d51e66c1b2ebc/pkg/k8s/apis/cilium.io/v2/ccnp_types.go#L101-L105). Retrieved implementation bytes matched the tag and immutable commit.

## Prism test lease requests an undeclared storage profile

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The default prism-e2e temporary-lease request writes spec.capabilityProfile: storage, but the declared BusterNamespaceLease spec has no such field. The namespace controller has no storage-profile selection for it.

Strict field validation can reject the lease request. A request that proceeds after unknown-field pruning still does not select a storage profile. A successful lease or Ready phase is insufficient evidence of persistence.

### Components and current state

- Prism end-to-end deploy command
- BusterNamespaceLease schema
- Namespace controller
- kubectl request validation

The producer and declared receiver disagree. Namespace ResourceQuota and LimitRange values are fixed controller settings. No product correction, live admission, volume provision or mount is established. The script installs its RETURN cleanup trap only after lease readiness and namespace verification, so earlier failure requires state inspection.

### Remaining work

- Owner: Prism maintainers, with the namespace-controller maintainer. Decide whether this producer should remove the unsupported field or whether a defined storage capability must be implemented and authorized.
- Align the producer, served schema, controller behavior and operator procedure. Preserve validation and namespace isolation; accepting an unknown field is not a capability implementation.
- Safe action: stop this lease-based exercise until the contract is repaired. If an attempt already ran, inspect the recorded lease and namespace before retry or cleanup.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Inspect cmd_prism_e2e in scripts/deploy.sh and the complete declared spec in the lease CRD. Confirm that the authored capabilityProfile field has no declared storage-profile receiver.
- Record the actual PATH kubectl version and installed CRD/server before diagnosing an attempted request. Distinguish a rejected write, pruned stored spec and authored text in the last-applied annotation.
- In a separately authorized isolated target, execute the repaired request and observe lease identity, namespace state and the claimed storage behavior. This target execution has not been performed.

### Completion criteria

- Producer, schema and controller agree on the complete supported lease input. Unknown-field validation and namespace authorization remain enforced.
- Local contract tests cover the corrected constructor and failure/cleanup boundaries; retain the exact source revision and outputs.
- In an isolated target, the declared storage behavior is observed with claim/volume identity, binding and mount evidence where persistence is promised. A Ready lease alone is not that proof.
- The operator guide and generated field reference describe the corrected input and its actual receiving authority.

### Separate environment acceptance

Actual target admission, controller reconciliation and any promised storage provisioning/mounting are separate product closure evidence. No live result is claimed.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Current evidence boundary

Current source shows the unsupported authored field and fixed namespace quota/limit settings. Unknown-field validation/pruning and actual client versions are separate receiving boundaries; this finding does not assume the executable or installed CRD of a previous run.

- **Observed behavior:** Live request acceptance and stored values remain unconfirmed.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.
